tasks.title: Implement first-run setup and profile settings
tasks.summary: Build the guided first-run and editable profile/ranking-settings screens for interests, starter sources, coarse location, optional demographics, and bounded signal controls.
tasks.objective: Let the user establish transparent local personalization without an account, automatic location, or inferred demographic values.
tasks.context: Explicit interests and source choices lead ranking. Country/region is manual; city, age, and gender are optional, local, disableable, and low-weight.
implementation_notes: Determine first-run state from authoritative API data, not a browser-local completed flag.
Present demographic fields after primary preferences and explain their optional, local, capped effect before entry.
Use separate enabled controls so clearing a value and disabling its ranking effect are understandable.
Do not request browser geolocation or perform IP-based location lookup.
acceptance_criteria: A new user can choose starter sources, enter interests, select country/region, optionally add city/age/gender, review signal controls, and save a valid local profile.
Age, gender, and city can be omitted; age/gender can be individually disabled and their capped influence is visible.
Invalid weights, locations, or profile fields show field-level contract errors without discarding valid unsaved entries.
Returning users bypass first-run setup and can edit or clear every accepted profile value.
No profile value is sent outside the same-origin local API or persisted as authoritative browser state.
verification: Run component tests for new, partial, valid, invalid, saved, and API-error states.
Run accessibility and keyboard tests for all fields, enable controls, validation summaries, and save feedback.
Run a browser test from empty profile through completed setup and reload.
Assert no browser geolocation/IP request and no authoritative profile persistence in browser storage.
tasks.handoff_notes: Feed ranking explanations must reflect the server's saved configuration rather than unsaved form state.

tasks.title: Implement source management and manual refresh
tasks.summary: Build source catalog/custom-source management, write-only credential controls, scraper policy visibility, refresh initiation, polling, and per-source outcome presentation.
tasks.objective: Let the user safely control what is ingested and understand refresh progress and failures without exposing secrets.
tasks.context: The MVP includes editable starter sources, manual RSS/API/approved-scraper configuration, and ingestion only while the executable runs.
implementation_notes: Show adapter type, enabled state, permission mode, credential configured state, and scraper policy status without displaying credential content.
Clear credential inputs immediately after successful submission, cancellation, route change, or component disposal.
Explain that refresh runs only while the app process is open.
Differentiate success, unchanged, partial success, failure, cancelled, conflict, and rate-limited outcomes.
acceptance_criteria: The user can enable/edit starter entries and add validated custom RSS, official API, or approved scraper source configurations.
Scraper configuration cannot appear enabled without required policy status and permission information from the API.
Credential UI supports configure/replace/delete and displays only configured/not-configured state.
One manual refresh can be started, duplicate-start conflict is explained, and polling stops at a terminal state.
Per-source counts and sanitized failures remain understandable after navigation or reload.
verification: Run component tests for every source kind, validation family, credential lifecycle, and deletion confirmation.
Run fake-timer tests for refresh polling and component disposal.
Run browser coverage from source creation through mixed-outcome refresh.
Run sentinel-secret checks across DOM, logs, caches, snapshots, and browser storage.
tasks.handoff_notes: Integration tests should use fictional fixtures; live provider setup remains an explicit later selection.

tasks.title: Implement the ranked feed and permission-aware reader
tasks.summary: Build the primary feed with pagination, filters, ranking explanations, article actions, refresh affordance, and an article reader that respects content permission mode.
tasks.objective: Deliver the core daily-use experience: see relevant news first, understand why, and read permitted content or open the publisher.
tasks.context: The backend owns score order and explanations. Hidden articles are excluded by default, and metadata-only articles must link out rather than render extracted full text.
implementation_notes: Preserve server order and display returned reason components without client-side score calculation.
Make publisher, publication time, permission mode, and outbound destination clear before navigation.
Render permitted content only through a reviewed sanitization boundary and block active markup/script execution.
Use mutation responses as authoritative and recover cleanly when optimistic interaction conflicts with server state.
acceptance_criteria: The default feed shows server-ranked non-hidden articles with stable pagination, source/date metadata, and concise truthful reasons.
The user can filter by source, read/unread, saved state, and accepted basic text/date options and can clear filters.
Read, save, and hide actions update visibly, survive query refresh, and expose accessible success/failure feedback.
Full-content-allowed articles render sanitized content; metadata-only articles never render a body and always provide the canonical publisher link.
Empty, initial loading, additional-page loading, stale/retry, partial-refresh, and API-unavailable states are distinct.
verification: Run component tests for feed ordering, filters, pagination, explanations, actions, and all status states.
Run malicious permitted-content fixtures through the reader and assert active content cannot execute.
Run browser coverage from refresh result to feed, explanation, reader/link-out, and inline actions.
Run accessibility tests for article lists, explanation disclosure, filters, and reader focus.
tasks.handoff_notes: The end-to-end acceptance flow should exercise this screen with persisted fixture data and a real local backend.

tasks.title: Implement personal library and settings integration
tasks.summary: Build saved/read/hidden library views, reversible state management, persistent filters, and cohesive links among library, profile, ranking, sources, and feed settings.
tasks.objective: Complete the persistent personal reading workflow and make all user-controlled ranking inputs discoverable and reversible.
tasks.context: The user selected read/unread, save-for-later, hide/dismiss, and basic filtering as MVP features. SQLite is authoritative across restarts.
implementation_notes: Store only disposable view/filter preferences in browser storage; retrieve all article/library state from the API.
Make hidden items intentionally discoverable in a management view so hide remains reversible.
Keep filter URL/query state understandable for back/forward navigation where practical.
After profile or ranking changes, show backend recomputation progress/stale state if the contract exposes it.
acceptance_criteria: Saved, read/unread, and hidden views load authoritative state and allow the accepted reversible actions.
Library state and server-backed filters survive application restart; disposable UI preferences may survive browser reload without becoming authoritative.
Restoring a hidden article makes it eligible for normal feed display after authoritative refresh.
Settings navigation clearly separates profile, ranking signals, sources, credentials, and refresh information.
The complete workflow remains usable by keyboard and presents useful empty/error states for each library view.
verification: Run component tests for saved, read/unread, hidden/restore, filters, reload, and error states.
Run browser coverage that changes actions, restarts/reloads the app, and confirms SQLite-backed persistence.
Inspect browser storage to confirm it contains no authoritative library records, profile data, article content, or credentials.
Run accessibility checks and keyboard-only action reversal.
edge_cases: Article state changes from another open tab
tasks.handoff_notes: Integration-release must prove the complete daily-use workflow across a real process restart, not only a browser reload.
